s-19-1-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. An Illustrative badge at 360 px with a check mark and the words “Fully accessible. This site works for everyone.” A note reads “No standard, no level, no date and no list of what was checked.”
s-19-1-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: a claim with no standard behind it.

s-19-2-correct.alt: An Illustrative pair at 360 px. First, the Voting symbol beside its word, “Voting”, marked with empty alt text because the word says it. Second, a bar chart titled “Comments on the county budget, 2023 to 2026”, its four bars rising from 120 comments in 2023 through 180 and 240 to 310 in 2026, each with its count above it and its year below, and a source line, with the alt text “Comments on the county budget rose each year, from 120 in 2023 to 310 in 2026.”
s-19-2-correct.notes: Correct: alt text for purpose, and empty alt where a word already says it. Invented counts.

s-19-2-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same Illustrative chart at 360 px, a bar chart titled “Comments on the county budget, 2023 to 2026”, its four bars rising from 120 comments in 2023 through 180 and 240 to 310 in 2026, each with its count above it and its year below, and a source line, with the alt text “chart_final_v2.png”, a file name. A note says a screen reader hears nothing of what the chart shows.
s-19-2-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: alt text that names a file. Invented counts.

s-19-3-correct.alt: An Illustrative comment form at 360 px with a field and two buttons, Start over and Send your comment. The instruction under it names the button by its words: “When your comment is ready, press Send your comment.”
s-19-3-correct.notes: Correct: an instruction that names the control by its words.

s-19-3-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same Illustrative form at 360 px, with the instruction “When your comment is ready, press the dark button on the right.”, which names no words.
s-19-3-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: an instruction by color and place alone (SC 1.3.3).

s-19-4-correct.alt: An Illustrative hinge headline at 360 px, “The zoning code & the rent.”, set as live text in White on a Prussian band, with a note that it grows, reflows and can be read aloud and translated.

s-19-4-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The Illustrative hinge headline “The zoning code & the rent.” at 360 px, set as a picture on a Prussian band, its letters soft at the edges. Under it, its first two letters, T and h, enlarged until each pixel shows as a square. A note says it cannot be found, translated or read aloud from its words.
s-19-4-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: a picture of text in place of text (SC 1.4.5).

s-19-5-correct.alt: An Illustrative line chart at 360 px, titled “Written comments and speakers at the county’s budget hearing, 2019 to 2026”, its two lines rising from 40 to 150 comments and from 20 to 40 speakers, each named with its last count at its end, the years 2019 and 2026 under it, and a source line. Under it, three buttons, Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit, each a single press.
s-19-5-correct.notes: Correct: every action is one press of a button. Invented counts.

s-19-5-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same Illustrative line chart at 360 px, titled “Written comments and speakers at the county’s budget hearing, 2019 to 2026”, its two lines rising from 40 to 150 comments and from 20 to 40 speakers, each named with its last count at its end, the years 2019 and 2026 under it, and a source line, with the line “Pinch to zoom. Drag to pan. Shake to undo. Press Z to zoom.” and no buttons.
s-19-5-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: gestures, motion and a single-key shortcut with no button (SC 2.1.4, 2.5.1, 2.5.4, 2.5.7). Invented counts.

s-19-6-correct.alt: A pair of buttons on a 360 px screen zoomed to 200 percent, drawn at twice true size: Previous page and Next page have stacked into one column, each word whole.
s-19-6-correct.notes: Correct: a row of two buttons that stacks as text grows. The 180 px layout a 360 px screen gives at 200 percent, drawn at exactly twice its sizes (scale 2).

s-19-6-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same buttons on a 360 px screen zoomed to 200 percent, drawn at twice true size and held side by side; their words may not wrap, so “Previous page” and “Next page” are cut off at the buttons’ edges.
s-19-6-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: labels that may not wrap (SC 1.4.4, 1.4.12). The 180 px layout a 360 px screen gives at 200 percent, drawn at exactly twice its sizes (scale 2).

s-19-7-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. An Illustrative report line at 360 px: “Automated scan: 0 errors. The page passes.” A note says one tool stood in for the whole matrix.
s-19-7-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: one automated score taken as a pass.

s-19-8-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. An Illustrative results line at 360 px: “Passes WCAG 2.2 AA on every browser and screen reader.” It has no date and mixes what was run with what was not.
s-19-8-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: a result with no date and no Not tested list.

s-19-9-failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. An Illustrative line at 360 px: “Checked with a screen reader. Looks fine.” A note says it names no device, screen reader, steps or date.
s-19-9-failure.notes: Picture of a fault: a device check no one could repeat.

s-19-criteria.alt: A searchable list of the 55 WCAG 2.2 success criteria at levels A and AA, in W3C’s words. Each entry gives the number, the name, the level, a tag for the six new in 2.2, the criterion’s words, and how this guide meets it: 33 are met by a rule, 8 in part, 9 are gaps with the chapter that owes each, and 5 govern things no product does today. A search field and a choice of All, Met, Met in part, Gaps or Not used today narrow the list, and a status line says how many show. A last line says 4.1.1 Parsing was removed in WCAG 2.2.
s-19-criteria.notes: Live: search and a radio choice filter the list; the count goes to a polite status line (Rule 18.15).

s-19-devices.alt: The device script, in four parts. iPhone with VoiceOver: 1. Open Settings, then Accessibility, then Accessibility Shortcut, and choose VoiceOver. From now on, pressing the side button three times, or the Home button on an iPhone that has one, turns VoiceOver on and off. 2. Open the page in Safari, then press that button three times. VoiceOver says “VoiceOver on”. 3. Swipe right with one finger to move to the next item, and left to go back. Each item is read aloud. 4. Double-tap anywhere to press the item VoiceOver is on. To type, double-tap a field, type, then swipe right to move on. 5. Go through the ten things to listen for below, and write Pass or Fail beside each with what you heard. 6. Press that button three times to turn VoiceOver off. Android phone with TalkBack: 1. Open Settings, then Accessibility, then TalkBack, and turn on the TalkBack shortcut. Makers name these menus differently; the shortcut is usually holding both volume keys for three seconds. 2. Open the page in Chrome, then hold both volume keys for three seconds. TalkBack says it is on. 3. Swipe right with one finger to move to the next item, and left to go back. Scroll with two fingers. 4. Double-tap anywhere to press the item TalkBack is on. To type, double-tap a field, type, then swipe right to move on. 5. Go through the ten things to listen for below, and write Pass or Fail beside each with what you heard. Gestures differ between TalkBack versions; Google’s TalkBack help lists the ones on your phone. 6. Hold both volume keys for three seconds to turn TalkBack off. Windows PC with NVDA and a contrast theme: 1. Download NVDA, a free screen reader, from nvaccess.org and install it. Start it from the Start menu; it says “NVDA started”. 2. Open the page in Chrome, Edge or Firefox. Press Tab to move from control to control, and Shift and Tab to go back. Press Enter or Space to press a control. Press Control to stop the speech. 3. Press H to jump from heading to heading, and D from landmark to landmark. 4. Go through the ten things to listen for below, and write Pass or Fail beside each with what you heard. Press Insert and Q, then Enter, to quit NVDA. 5. Now turn on a contrast theme: on Windows 11, open Settings, then Accessibility, then Contrast themes, choose Night sky and press Apply. On Windows 10, open Settings, then Ease of Access, then High contrast. 6. Reload the page and look: every button keeps an edge, the focus ring shows on each Tab stop, a pressed chip keeps its check, an error keeps its bar, and the warning and success marks stay visible. Write down any that vanish, then set the theme back to None. Mac with VoiceOver: 1. In Safari, open Settings, then Advanced, and turn on “Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage”. 2. Press Command and F5 to turn VoiceOver on. It says “VoiceOver on Safari”. 3. Press Tab to move from control to control, and Shift and Tab to go back. Press Control, Option and the Right Arrow to read the next item, and Control, Option and Space to press it. 4. Press Control, Option and U to open the rotor, a list of the page’s headings, links and landmarks. The Left and Right Arrows switch lists, the Up and Down Arrows choose, and Return goes there. 5. Go through the ten things to listen for below, and write Pass or Fail beside each with what you heard. 6. Press Command and F5 to turn VoiceOver off. Ten things to listen for: 1. The page’s title is read as the page opens. 2. The first stop is “Skip to main content”. 3. Headings come in order: the page’s title first, then each part under it. 4. Each control says its words and what kind of control it is, and a pressed, checked or current one says so. 5. A button that waits says it is unavailable and why. 6. The phone menu takes you inside when it opens, and Close the menu, or Escape on a keyboard, brings you back to Menu. 7. Typing in a search field, you hear how many results there are, and the cursor stays in the field. 8. Pressing Copy, you hear what was copied. 9. Sending a form with a mistake takes you to the field to fix, and you hear the error. 10. Nothing you cannot see is read, and nothing you cannot see takes focus.
s-19-devices.notes: Readable: the device script of DR-213, four devices, each step numbered, with what a pass sounds like.

s-19-matrix.alt: The verification matrix: 15 checks, each with what it shows, its method, the WCAG 2.2 criteria it serves and, where a tool runs it, how. Every page rendered: Screenshots at 1440, 1024, 390 and 360 px, looked at by a person. Report pages: A screenshot of each page in the report reader. Keyboard and focus: A script presses Tab through the page, walks each component’s keyboard path and measures each control’s size; a person checks the order and the ring. Reading order and headings: The accessibility tree’s outline, read by script and by a person. Forms and messages: Send each form empty, then with a mistake, by keyboard: focus lands on the first field to fix, its description holds the message, and the status line holds the result. Automated rules: axe-core with the tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa on every page. Contrast: A script reads each rendered color pair, states included; a person measures marks, edges and rings against 3 to 1. Text at 200 percent and 320 px: Text doubled, the page at 320 px, then line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2 times the size, letter spacing 0.12 and word spacing 0.16 times the size, all at once. A script finds sideways scroll and clipped boxes, and a person reads for words broken in the middle. Reduced motion: The browser set to reduce motion, then each moving part played. Forced colors: The browser set to forced colors, light and dark, then each part read by script and by eye. Dark surfaces and long labels: Each part on Newsprint, Charcoal and any other surface it uses, filled with the longest real words it will hold, such as the longest title in its data. Print: Print emulation and the print stylesheet: every word prints, in reading order, and nothing is cut at a page’s edge. Downloads: Press each download, open each file, check SVG validity and PNG size. Diagram and chart equivalents: Each drawing checked for its words or table and its reading guide. Grayscale: Grayscale screenshots of every page, with each state shown.
s-19-matrix.notes: Readable: the checks and methods of the verification matrix, with what each shows.

s-19-opener.alt: Where this guide stands on WCAG 2.2’s 55 criteria at levels A and AA: 33 met, where a rule states what the criterion asks; 8 met in part; 9 gaps, each with the chapter that owes it; and 5 not used today, since no product does what they cover yet.
s-19-opener.notes: Chapter 19’s opener (CD-S18, D2-1550): the counts from Rule 19.1’s map, as a picture that flows with the column at true size.

s-19-results.alt: The guide’s own results, November 11, 2026. The chapters page as built at 08:40 UTC from commit 04a3f3b8’s generator chain: chapters 01 to 12, 17, 18, 19 and 26, 185 rules, 424 specimens, 8,962,864 bytes, with no build warning, checked in Chromium at 1440, 1024, 390 and 360 px. Tested: Automated rules: axe-core 4.10.2 with the tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa found no violation at any of the four widths, with its color-contrast rule run outside the plates marked as contrast failures. Contrast: No text measured under 4.5 to 1, or 3 to 1 for large text, outside the labeled failure plates, and no text under 13 px, at all four widths. The token tests found every role that carries a contrast threshold at or over it on each surface it serves. Keyboard and focus: The first 60 Tab stops at 1440 and 390 px each showed a focus ring. All 37 keyboard paths of chapter 18’s 24 components and chapter 26’s download passed: 140 walks and 714 steps, in both themes at 1440 and 390 px. Each Clear the search control that shows only after typing measured 44 by 44 px, and the masthead’s phone menu opened, held focus, closed by Escape and by Close, and returned focus, at 390 and 360 px. Reading order and headings: 268 headings with one h1, no skipped level and none inside a specimen, at every width. Forms and messages: Chapter 18’s form, sent by keyboard with two mistakes in both themes at 1440 and 390 px, moved focus to the first field to fix, marked both fields invalid and showed the message; sent right, its button read “Sending” and its status line said the reader was signed up. Text at 200 percent and 320 px: At the default text size no width scrolled sideways outside a scroll frame. With text at 200 percent at 1024, 390 and 360 px, and with WCAG’s text spacing at 390 and 360 px, the page did not scroll sideways and no control clipped its words. Reduced motion: All 7 moving specimens stayed still on load, came to rest after Play, and with reduced motion on showed their final frame at once. Forced colors: With forced colors emulated at each width, 590 to 593 glyph parts kept their contrast, and the masthead’s wordmark drew in one color in the dark and the light palette. Dark surfaces: With the device set to dark, all 67,481 elements kept their light colors, so the guide stays on Newsprint. No Pillar Red pixel sat within 2 px of a Prussian one in any of 480 stages at 1440 px, both themes of each live component included, and again after Send was pressed in 3 of 3 forms. Code to copy: Each of the 28 code sets, pasted into a blank page with tokens.css, drew as its live stage in both themes at all four widths: 30 to 43 of the 56 stages pixel for pixel, the rest within the measured tolerance at curve edges and rows a pixel apart, and a comparison of 2,152 elements’ computed styles found no difference. Drawings at each screen density: Every civic line, pillar, fit and utility drawing in the page’s sprite drew as its master at 1x and 2x, with a largest difference of 0, and each of the 41 drawings that switch showed its 24 px fit alone at 1x and 1.5x and its master alone at 2x. Not tested: Every page rendered: The check saved one capture of each section at 1440 and 390 px; this record holds no look by a person at every chapter at all four widths. Report pages: No report exists yet; chapter 24 brings the first. 320 px: The check’s narrowest width is 360 px. Long labels: No run filled the components with the atlas’s longest titles. Print: Not run on this build. Downloads: The token download test was not among this build’s runs. Diagram and chart equivalents: Not checked by script; chapters 14 and 15, which hold most drawings, are not written yet. Grayscale: Not run on this build. Screen readers, real phones, Safari, Firefox and Windows contrast themes: The machine these checks ran on has none of them; the device script of Rule 19.9 covers them before launch. Keyboard order and reading order by a person: Only scripts walked them on this build.
s-19-results.notes: Readable: printed from 20261111_Stage-C-Round-2-Ch19-Results.json, which names the runs behind each line.
